questions.prompt: Two runs with the same seed give different results because the code iterates over a set of sensor names. The root cause is
options: string hash randomization changes set iteration order between processes
Python ignores the seed unless it is also passed to every function call
floating-point addition is random, so each run sums the readings differently
sets keep insertion order, but the seed resets it after every import
questions.explanation: PYTHONHASHSEED salts string hashes; sort before iterating.

questions.prompt: Which belongs inside the hashed result file of an experiment?
options: the wall-clock time of the run
the absolute path of the output folder
questions.explanation: Anything that varies between identical runs belongs in separate metadata.

questions.prompt: A logging setup function that adds a handler on every call is called 4 times. How many copies of each message appear?
Per-run standard deviation of an estimator is 0.02. The mean over 25 seeds has what standard error?
Why use a local random.Random(seed) object instead of the global random.seed?
options: the global generator cannot be seeded once any other module has imported random
results no longer depend on the order of unrelated calls that draw random numbers
it avoids importing the random module, so no other code can change its state
local generators are faster than the global one because they skip the module lock
questions.explanation: Explicit generator state is an explicit input.

questions.prompt: How many characters are in the canonical JSON string {"a":1,"b":2} (sorted keys, no spaces)?
A colleague cannot reproduce your reported result from your repository. Describe the clean-checkout test you would run, what you compare, and which differences are acceptable.
rubric: Clones into a new directory, creates a fresh environment from pinned dependencies and runs with the saved config.
Compares a hash or tolerance-based metrics of the result files.
Accepts only differences in metadata (time, host, paths) and flags result differences as failures.
